notes:

FAA-G-ACS-2 (Companion Guide) at revision C.

title: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards
notes:
Supersedes FAA-S-ACS-6B. Non-regulatory appendix material moved to
FAA-G-ACS-2 (Companion Guide) at revision C.

title: FAA Chief Counsel Legal Interpretations (index)
notes:
Watcher entry, not a document. The list check flags when new
interpretations appear so individual ones can be catalogued.

title: Legal Interpretation to Peter H. Asp
notes:
Whether commercial balloon training can be logged before holding a private
certificate, whether the commercial knowledge test can be taken first, and
how the two § 61.129(h)(4) solo-flight provisions fit together. Corrects
and strikes the May 12, 2015 letter to the same requester.

title: Legal Interpretation to Daniel Beard
notes:
Whether subpart C student solo endorsements apply to certificated pilots
adding a category or class, whether a § 61.31(d) endorsement expires, and
whether the solo pilot needs a current flight review.

title: Legal Interpretation to Chris Bennett (Southern California Soaring Academy)
notes:
Follow-up to Beard: flight review for certificated pilots soloing in a new
category, whether a § 61.87 student endorsement may be used instead of
§ 61.31(d), and whether limits can be written into a § 61.31(d) endorsement.
Includes the requester's email and sample glider endorsements.

title: Chief Counsel Memorandum to R. C. Carty, AFX-1: Reconsideration of Glaser (2008) and Pratte (2012)
notes:
Rescinds the Glaser and Pratte interpretations on the three-approach IFR
cross-country under § 61.65(d)(2)(ii)(C), including their treatment of PAR
and ASR. Refers the navigation-system question to Flight Standards.

title: Legal Interpretation to David Cleveland
notes:
What documentation a private applicant needs for home-study ground training,
required wording of the knowledge-test endorsement, and whether § 61.107
areas of operation must be listed verbatim in the logbook.

title: Legal Interpretation to Glenn D. Counsil
notes:
Whether an airline first officer may log PIC as sole manipulator, and the
effect of an "SIC Privileges Only" type rating. Footnote corrects the 1999
Carpenter regional interpretation.

title: Legal Interpretation to Mr. Creech
notes:
Who logs PIC and SIC when one pilot flies under a view-limiting device and
the other is safety pilot, depending on which one acts as PIC.

title: Legal Interpretation to B. Dan Crowe (Palm Beach Helicopters)
notes:
Commercial airplane pilot adding a helicopter rating: crediting time
performing PIC duties with an instructor, logging PIC when not rated, and
whether a § 61.31(d) endorsement is needed for that time.

title: Legal Interpretation to B. Dan Crowe Jr. (Palm Beach Helicopters)
notes:
Whether a part 141 end-of-course test given under examining authority is a
practical test for medical-certificate purposes.

title: Legal Interpretation to B. Dan Crowe Jr. (Palm Beach Helicopters)
notes:
Five questions on when a private applicant needs a medical certificate:
examiner acting as PIC, part 141 end-of-course tests, issuing the
certificate, training without a medical, and a "student pilot purposes
only" medical.

title: Legal Interpretation to Francis De Joseph
notes:
Whether § 91.405(c) and § 91.213(d)(2) let a part 91 aircraft operate
indefinitely with inoperative equipment.

title: Legal Interpretation to Ian Robert Dean (Dean International)
notes:
Whether a multiengine airplane may be used for the complex portion of a
commercial single-engine practical test, or for the § 61.129(a)(3)(ii)
complex training hours. Cites Fitch (Nov. 14, 2012).

title: Chief Counsel Memorandum to Ricardo Domingo, AFX-1: 14 CFR 67.401(f)(4)
notes:
Whether an unexpired special-issuance Authorization can be withdrawn for not
providing medical information after the underlying medical certificate has
expired, and the effect on BasicMed eligibility. Includes the AFS request memo.

title: Chief Counsel Memorandum to Ricardo Domingo, AFX-1: 14 CFR 61.109(a)
notes:
Whether the 20 hours of dual and 10 hours of solo in § 61.109(a) must be in a
single-engine airplane and include the (a)(1)-(5) training. Requested by
Flight Standards; includes the AFS-800 request memo.

title: Legal Interpretation to Jeff Gebhart
notes:
PIC and cross-country logging for a pilot under the hood and the safety
pilot acting as PIC on a 187 nm flight.

title: Legal Interpretation to Ted Louis Glenn
notes:
Seven scenarios on logging PIC, SIC and cross-country time across safety
pilot, part 135 and part 121 crews, and shared flying; plus whether a
repositioning flight changes the original point of departure.

title: Legal Interpretation to Gareth Gordon
notes:
Whether the § 61.65(d) 50 hours of PIC cross-country and 40 hours of
instrument time may be accrued concurrently.

title: Legal Interpretation to William Grannis
notes:
Whether cross-country time is logged as airborne time or as "flight time"
under § 1.1. Includes the request letter, which raises examiners
discounting cross-country time.

title: Legal Interpretation to William Grannis
notes:
Whether the § 61.129(a)(4) 10 hours may combine solo time and time
performing PIC duties with an instructor. Includes the request letter.

title: Legal Interpretation to William W. Grannis
notes:
Meaning of "student instruction" and "training flights" in § 119.1(e),
and how discovery, introductory and demonstration flights fit the
exceptions, including the air tour LOA route.

title: Legal Interpretation to Taylor Grayson
notes:
Whether a CFII without a multiengine rating on the flight instructor
certificate may give instrument training in a multiengine airplane, and the
2009 change to § 61.195(c). Notes Order 8900.1 5-503 as inconsistent.

title: Legal Interpretation to Taylor Grayson
notes:
Whether a CFI without an instrument rating may give training toward the
instrument rating beyond the required 15 hours, and which solo
endorsements a CFI must keep records of under § 61.189(b)(1).

title: Legal Interpretation to Taylor Grayson
notes:
Whether the § 61.31(e)-(j) additional training and endorsements are
"ratings limitations" that § 61.31(l)(2) waives for student pilots and
practical test applicants.

title: Legal Interpretation to Stephen R. Greenwood (Fly By Knight)
notes:
Six scenarios on the 100-hour inspection for an aircraft used for both
instruction and rental, the 10-hour en-route allowance, and whether an
annual resets the 100-hour clock. Corrects and strikes the Oct. 1, 2014
letter to the same requester.

title: Legal Interpretation to Randy Haralson
notes:
Whether dual time in actual instrument conditions, as sole manipulator,
counts toward the 50 hours of cross-country time as PIC for the instrument
rating.

title: Legal Interpretation to Kristine Hartzell (AOPA)
notes:
Clarifies the Oct. 8, 2010 Theriault letter on whether instrument rating
training satisfies the commercial instrument aeronautical experience.

title: Legal Interpretation to Jason E. Herman
notes:
Whether a rated pilot without complex or high-performance endorsements may
log PIC as sole manipulator. Source of the logging-PIC versus acting-as-PIC
distinction cited in later letters.

title: Legal Interpretation to James Hilliard
notes:
Whether two pilots who split a flight at the controls may each log
cross-country time toward § 61.65(d).

title: Legal Interpretation to Joseph S. Jablecki
notes:
Whether the CFI giving the five hours of helicopter control by reference to
instruments under § 61.129(c)(3)(i) needs an instrument rating on the
flight instructor certificate.

title: Legal Interpretation to Terrence K. Keller Jr.
notes:
Whether the private long solo cross-country must also meet the § 61.1
cross-country definition, worked through a three-airport example.

title: Legal Interpretation to Jared Kuhn
notes:
How the CFI and the applicant log time spent performing PIC duties with an
instructor under § 61.129(a)(4), and who must act as PIC.

title: Legal Interpretation to Thomas D. Letts
notes:
Whether a C172 may fly VFR day on strobes alone with the rotating beacon
placarded inoperative.

title: Legal Interpretation to Ronald B. Levy
notes:
Whether a CFII instructing in actual conditions may log the student's
approaches toward the instructor's own § 61.57(c) currency.

title: Legal Interpretation to Bryan McLellan
notes:
Whether a commercial helicopter rating can be sought without a private
helicopter rating, whether commercial-level training logged before adding
the private rating still counts, and the 20 hours for a category add-on.

title: Legal Interpretation to Jeff Morgan
notes:
Whether a pilot with an SIC-privileges-only type rating may log PIC as sole
manipulator. Restates Counsil.

title: Legal Interpretation to Daniel Murphy
notes:
Five questions: medical class for a CFI instructing for hire, student solo
above a cloud layer, what counts as a logbook, introductory flights under
§ 119.1(e)(1), and shoulder harness during taxi. Withdraws the 1991 Gandy
and Rubin interpretations.

title: Legal Interpretation to Daniel Murphy
notes:
Right turns on a circling approach at a Class G airport, logging PIC on a
practical test, and how far an approach must be flown to count for
currency and the instrument rating.

title: Legal Interpretation to Daniel Murphy
notes:
When anticollision lights must be on and whether both beacon and strobes
are required; and whether a student pilot's cross-country can count for the
commercial 2-hour day cross-country.

title: Legal Interpretation to Daniel Murphy
notes:
AIM right-turn pattern entry versus § 91.126 (refers to Krug 2014 and
Gossman 2011), logging PIC while using the autopilot, and double-logging
PIC and SIC.

title: Legal Interpretation to Richard L. Newman
notes:
Whether a flight review may be split between two instructors, and whether a
certificated pilot needs a current flight review to solo while training for
a glider rating.

title: Legal Interpretation to Mr. O'Mara
notes:
Which § 61.109(j) weight-shift-control experience must be in a WSC aircraft
when adding the rating to an existing private certificate.

title: Legal Interpretation to David J. Oord (AOPA)
notes:
Reconciles Theriault (2010, 2011), Hartzell (2010) and Jablecki (2016) on
counting instrument-rating training toward § 61.129 and states they remain
in effect. Includes the AFS-810 inquiry.

title: Legal Interpretation to Richard A. Peri (Aircraft Electronics Association)
notes:
Meaning of "inspected" in § 91.405(c) for equipment left inoperative under
§ 91.213(d). Includes the AEA request.

title: Legal Interpretation to Samuel T. Ragland (Double Eagle Aviation)
notes:
Meaning of "necessary training" in § 61.49(a)(1) after a failed practical
test, and who decides what retraining is required.

title: Legal Interpretation to Samuel T. Ragland (Double Eagle Aviation)
notes:
Whether the § 119.1(e)(4) aerial-work exception covers sightseeing flights
without a § 91.147 LOA or part 119 certificate.

title: Legal Interpretation to Norman W. Robinson Jr.
notes:
Whether the 80 hours of instruction required to train initial glider CFI
applicants must have been given in gliders.

title: Legal Interpretation to Scott Rohlfing
notes:
Whether the private pilot's 3 hours of control by reference to instruments
count toward the instrument rating's 40 hours and 15 hours.

title: Legal Interpretation to E. Thomas Sisk
notes:
Whether a cross-country flight must include a single leg of more than 50 nm.
Reaffirms Tenuta (Apr. 17, 1998).

title: Legal Interpretation to John Speranza
notes:
Whether a non-instrument-rated pilot may log PIC as sole manipulator on an IFR
flight, and whether the instrument-rated pilot acting as PIC may also log it.

title: Legal Interpretation to Mike Sun
notes:
Whether a commercial helicopter night cross-country under IFR can also count
toward the instrument portion of § 61.129(c)(3).

title: Legal Interpretation to Richard Theriault
notes:
Follow-up to the Oct. 8, 2010 Theriault letter: devices usable for the
§ 61.129(c)(3)(i) hours, and whether a part 135 company instructor without a
CFI is an authorized instructor for logbook entries and the 8710.

title: Legal Interpretation to William F. Trussell
notes:
How a safety pilot logs time depending on who acts as PIC, and whether the
safety pilot must share expenses under § 61.113(c).

title: Legal Interpretation to Peter K. Underwood
notes:
Whether instructors under 24 months may train or retrain an initial CFI
applicant, and whether a CFI who gave no flight training may sign the
§ 61.187 endorsement and the 8710. Cites Order 8900.1 and 8900.2.

title: Legal Interpretation to Dwight B. Van Zanen
notes:
Whether a pilot may choose how to divide legs into separate flights when
logging cross-country time.

title: Legal Interpretation to Troy M. Wadsworth (National Pilot Academy)
notes:
Whether an initial CFI applicant may get "right seat proficient" with a
junior instructor before training with a § 61.195(h) instructor.

title: Legal Interpretation to Keith E. Walker
notes:
Whether a non-instrument-rated pilot flying in IMC may log PIC and actual
instrument time while an instrument-rated pilot acts as PIC.

title: Legal Interpretation to Stephen J. Williams
notes:
Whether a gyroplane may be flown under IFR or below VFR minimums without an
instrument rating. Includes the request letter.

title: Legal Interpretation to Lawrence Williams
notes:
Whether a CFI not acting as PIC needs a medical when training a single-engine
pilot for a multiengine rating, and whether instrument training may be
given from a jump seat with a safety pilot up front.

title: Legal Interpretation to Joshua Wynne
notes:
Whether a newly instrument-rated pilot is immediately subject to the
§ 61.57(c) recency requirement.

title: Designee Management Policy
notes:
Revision E cancels 8000.95D (dated January 21, 2025). Ten volumes:
Vol 1 is common policy for all AVS designees (application, oversight,
annual extension, termination, suspension); Vol 3 is the DPE, SAE and
Admin PE policy. Vol 1 Ch 1 para 7 lists the changes by volume.

title: Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 1 Sec 3 — Phases of Certification
notes:
Vol 5 Ch 1: Direction, Guidance, and Procedures for Title 14 CFR Parts 121/135 and General Aviation.
Paras 5-51 through 5-58. 8710-1 review is 5-53, 8400-3 review is 5-54,
applicant identity verification is 5-55, drug convictions is 5-56. 5-57 and
5-58 cover the oral and flight test phases for Parts 121 and 135.

title: Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 2 Sec 1 — General
notes:
Vol 5 Ch 2: Title 14 CFR Part 61 Certification of Pilots and Flight Instructors.
Paras 5-216 through 5-223. Certification process and SODA in 5-218
(SODA at 5-218F). Aircraft, equipment, limitations, and FSTDs in 5-219.
SRM evaluation in 5-220. Plan of action in 5-221: PTS-based tests at B,
ACS-based tests at C, worked ACS example at D, designee location at E.
Pretest, preflight, and postflight briefings in 5-222. Combination practical
tests in 5-223, including discontinuance (H), disapproval notice (I), and
retest after failure (K).

title: Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 2 Sec 11 — Conduct a Title 14 CFR Part 61 Flight Instructor Initial Certification, Additional Category/Class Ratings, Recent Experience Validation, and Reinstatement of Privileges
notes:
Vol 5 Ch 2: Title 14 CFR Part 61 Certification of Pilots and Flight Instructors.
Paras 5-496 through 5-511, in the standard task layout.

title: Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 2 Sec 12 — Conduct a Title 14 CFR Part 61 Flight Instructor with a Sport Pilot Rating Initial Certification, Additional Category/Class Privilege, Recent Experience Validation, or Reinstatement of Privileges
notes:

notes:
Vol 5 Ch 2: Title 14 CFR Part 61 Certification of Pilots and Flight Instructors.
Paras 5-701 through 5-715, in the standard task layout.

Vol 5 Ch 2: Title 14 CFR Part 61 Certification of Pilots and Flight Instructors.
Paras 5-236 through 5-240. Simulated power failure dangers 5-237, scan
program 5-238, position reporting and collision avoidance 5-239, instrument

title: Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 2 Sec 24 — Conduct a Sport Pilot Certification, Including Additional Category/Class Privilege

title: Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 2 Sec 3 — Flight Reviews and Competency Checks
notes:
Vol 5 Ch 2: Title 14 CFR Part 61 Certification of Pilots and Flight Instructors.
Paras 5-256 through 5-269. Evaluating the review 5-262, length 5-263,

high-performance and complex checks 5-266 and 5-267, NVG 5-269.

notes:

Paras 5-286 through 5-292. Procedures 5-288, references and job aids 5-289,

notes:

5-313, English language requirements 5-314, hearing- and speech-impaired

notes:
Vol 5 Ch 2: Title 14 CFR Part 61 Certification of Pilots and Flight Instructors.
Paras 5-371 through 5-384, in the standard task layout (reporting system,

title: Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 2 Sec 8 — Conduct a Commercial Pilot Certification Including Additional Category/Class Ratings
notes:
Vol 5 Ch 2: Title 14 CFR Part 61 Certification of Pilots and Flight Instructors.
Paras 5-401 through 5-411, in the standard task layout.

notes:
